title: Symbiotic stream adapters: dual-consumer ergonomics and resumable WebStream <> AsyncIterator examples
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: TypeScript SDK consumers need clear, ergonomic primitives to interoperate between Web Streams (ReadableStream) and AsyncIterator/AsyncIterable consumers for LLM streaming responses. Existing guides scattered across PRs focus on single-consumer patterns or resume semantics independently. This ticket implements a set of lightweight 'symbiotic adapters' that: 1) allow two consumer styles to attach to the same logical response stream (dual-consumer) without duplicating memory/KV cache, 2) propagate backpressure and cancellation in a predictable way, and 3) support idempotent resume via checkpoint tokens for retryable network errors.

Scope: Design and implement adapters + runtime helpers in the TypeScript SDK, add canonical examples, unit + integration tests, and a short migration guide for customers. Provide small sample app and a cookbook page. Deliverables: adapter API (StreamHandle), dual-consumer demo example, resume token helper, backpressure mapping tests, docs/examples and a GitHub PR.

Why unique: Instead of merely converting between AsyncIterator and ReadableStream, the symbiotic adapters expose a shared interior buffer and controlled handoff semantics so both consumers can consume without race conditions or double-decoding. They also expose a tiny resume token interface allowing safe reconnect logic for transient failures (important for long-running chat streams).
acceptance_criteria: A TypeScript API (StreamHandle) exists that can expose a single underlying transport stream to both an AsyncIterator consumer and a ReadableStream consumer concurrently.
Backpressure from either consumer correctly influences the shared producer (unit tests that simulate slow consumer and fast producer).
Resumable checkpoint tokens produced by the adapter allow resume from network interruption without data duplication or violating order semantics (integration test against a recorded server fixture).
Examples folder contains 'dual-consumer-demo.ts' and 'resume-reconnect-example.ts' with runnable instructions.
Documentation page (SDK docs/cookbook) added with migration notes and recommended patterns.
At least one review approval from SDK maintainers and passing CI (unit + integration tests added to pipeline).
notes: Design decision: use a small shared ring buffer with configurable max entries (default 64) to avoid unbounded memory use; trade-off is additional copying but simplifies consistency guarantees.
Trade-off: exposing 'dual-consumer' is intentionally opinionated — we prefer a supported primitive over encouraging ad-hoc cloning, which caused subtle ordering bugs for customers.
Retry semantics: resume token encodes last output token index + stream-offset checksum; this keeps tokens small and avoids shipping entire KV cache state to the client.
Compatibility: adapters implemented in plain TS with no DOM-only APIs to keep Node/Deno/browser parity; ReadableStream polyfill used in tests for Node 18 compatibility.
Performance: microbenchmarks show ~3-7% CPU overhead versus raw async iterator for short streams, but negligible for long-running chat (cost justified by ergonomics).
